The widening of the confidence intervals across the different time horizons directly reflects my assessment of increasing uncertainty as we look further into the future. While my confidence intervals account for a range of typical fluctuations, specific unforeseen risks or "black swan" events could push outcomes beyond these stated boundaries. Conversely, a breakthrough technological innovation or a highly positive geopolitical resolution could trigger a substantial upward surge. Other potential disruptors include major natural disasters, unexpected regulatory changes impacting the underlying sector, or a sudden, severe supply chain shock. These types of low-probability, high-impact events are difficult to fully quantify within standard confidence intervals and represent the primary risks for outcomes outside my forecast range.
